title: Migrate to cashu-ts v4
body:
## Summary

- Upgraded cashu-ts from v3.5 to v4.3.0
- Number-typed amount boundary: introduces `AppMintQuote` / `AppMeltQuote` types and conversion helpers (`amountToNumber`, `toProofs`, `toMeltQuote`) at the store boundary so the rest of the app continues to work with number amounts.
- Shared `CounterSource`: a single ephemeral counter source is shared across wallet instances, with countersReserved events persisting advances to localStorage immediately. This replaces the old manual counter pre-bump/rollback workaround for melt operations and adds `retryOnceOnSignedOutputs` as a safety net.
- Type fixes in touched paths: removes `as any` casts encountered during the migration; properly types `StoredMint`, `WalletProof`, `DexieProofRow`.
- Fixes latent restore bug where restore never advanced the keyset counter, causing "outputs already signed" errors on the next operation until repeated +10 bumps caught up.
- Removes dead (disabled) Token v3 code
- Housekeeping: removes dead `src/boot/cashu.js` and its Quasar boot entry; excludes @cashu/cashu-ts from Vite dep optimizer (ESM + BigInt); adds sumProofAmounts helper; renames token.decode to token.decodeMeta; adds i18n `trying_again` key and translations; adds wallet store tests for counter and melt flows.

## NOTES

- Cashu-TS requires Node >=22.4.0 for full websocket support. Engine and CI updated to reflect this

## Test plan

- [x] Mint sats via Lightning invoice
- [x] Send/receive Cashu tokens (swap, redeem + trusted mint paths)
- [x] Pay Lightning invoice (melt)
- [x] Kill tab during melt, reopen — no "outputs already signed" error
- [x] Multi-mint swap
- [x] Restore wallet from mnemonic — counter recovery
- [x] P2PK locked send/receive
- [x] npm test passes

title: feat: migrate core wallet operations to @cashu/coco-core
body:
# Cashu.me Coco Migration Plan

## Completed
- **Initialization**: Integrated `@cashu/coco-core` and `@cashu/coco-indexeddb`. Created `src/stores/coco.ts` and `src/boot/coco.ts` to manage the core `Manager` instance.
- **Data Migration**: Added a one-time startup script (`src/js/migrate-to-coco.ts`) to migrate legacy `localStorage` mints and `Dexie.js` proofs into the new IndexedDB schema.
- **Proofs & Balances**: Updated `src/stores/proofs.ts` to drop `Dexie.js` live queries and instead read from `cocoStore.manager.repos.proofRepository`. Listens to Coco's Typed Event Bus (`proofs:saved`, `proofs:state-changed`, etc.) to trigger reactive UI updates.
- **Minting**: Replaced custom polling and `requestMint`/`mintOnPaid` flows in `CreateInvoiceDialog.vue` with `manager.ops.mint.prepare()`, `manager.subscription.awaitMintQuotePaid()`, and `manager.ops.mint.execute()`.
- **Melting / Paying**: Refactored `meltInvoiceData` and `meltQuoteInvoiceData` in `wallet.ts` via patch files to utilize `manager.ops.melt.prepare()` and `execute()`.
- **Swaps**: Rewrote `mintAmountSwap` and `meltProofsToMint` in `swap.ts` to execute sequential `mint.prepare()` + `melt.prepare()` operations over Coco.
- **Receiving Tokens**: Replaced manual token decoding, validation, and secret extraction in `receiveTokensStore.ts` with `manager.ops.receive.prepare()` and `execute()`.
- **History Tracking**: Disabled legacy manual `localStorage` tracking (`historyTokens` and `invoiceHistory`). Rewrote `HistoryTable.vue` to fetch data asynchronously via `manager.history.getPaginatedHistory()`.
- **NWC / Nostr Connect**: Updated `handlePayInvoice` and `handleMakeInvoice` in `nwc.ts` to use Coco APIs. Hooked into `FinalizedMeltOperation` effective fees to accurately deduct NWC allowances.
- **Worker Cleanup**: Disabled custom legacy polling loops (`invoicesWorker.ts`) to let Coco's background `MintOperationWatcher` handle invoice orchestration.

## Remaining to be done
- **Sending Tokens (Offline/Inband)**: Refactor `src/stores/sendTokensStore.ts` and `SendTokenDialog.vue` to completely replace the legacy manual proof extraction and JSON encoding process with `manager.ops.send.prepare()` and `execute()`. Ensure proper handling of pending vs offline tokens.
- **Multi-nut Payments**: Ensure the multi-mint paying feature (`MultinutPaymentDialog.vue`) integrates cleanly with `manager.ops.melt` using multiple mints simultaneously.
- **Nostr Peer-to-Peer Sending (NIP-17/NIP-04)**: `nostr.ts` still has some hardcoded token creation. It needs to utilize `ops.send.prepare()` before DMing tokens to users.
- **Legacy Store Deletion**: Completely purge the old custom functions from `src/stores/wallet.ts` (currently many are left commented out or orphaned) to drastically reduce bundle size and code clutter.
- **Legacy Storage Purge**: Safely drop the `cashuDb` initialization from `dexie.ts` entirely once confident in the migration logic, and stop hydrating `historyTokens` to localStorage.
- **Complete Test Coverage Update**: Fix any remaining legacy mocks in `src/stores/__tests__/wallet.test.js` that might conflict with the new Coco patterns.

title: fix(nostr): respect verbose flag in backup error notifications
body: When adding a mint from the discovery page, users see two notifications in sequence: 1. ✅ "Mint saved successfully" (expected) 2. ❌ "Failed to backup mint list to Nostr: No relay was able to receive the event." (unexpected) The mint is successfully saved, but the error notification creates a confusing user experience, making it appear as if something went wrong even though the primary operation (adding the mint) completed successfully. The issue occurs in `src/stores/nostrMintBackup.ts` in the `backupMintsToNostr()` function. When a mint is added, it triggers an automatic Nostr backup with `verbose=false`, but the error handler always shows an error notification regardless of the `verbose` flag. This means automatic background backup failures display error notifications to users, even though the primary operation (adding the mint) succeeded. **File**: `src/stores/nostrMintBackup.ts` **Function**: `backupMintsToNostr(verbose: boolean = false)` **Issue**: Error notification is shown even when `verbose=false` ## Solution Made error notifications conditional on the `verbose` parameter. Now: - **Automatic backups** (called with `verbose=false`): Fail silently, errors logged to console only - **Manual backups** (called with `verbose=true`): Show error notifications when they fail The fix ensures that automatic background backup failures don't interrupt users with error notifications, while manual backup operations still provide feedback when they fail.

title: feat: auto-rebalancer
body:
# Auto-Rebalance Feature

## Overview

The auto-rebalance feature helps users maintain balanced token distribution across multiple mints by automatically detecting imbalances and prompting the user to rebalance when needed.

## How It Works

### Balance Detection

The system monitors mint balances and calculates whether they fall outside user-defined target ranges:

1. User sets target percentages for each mint via sliders in the UI
2. Percentages are automatically normalized to sum to 100%
3. After minting or receiving tokens, the system checks if any mint's actual balance differs from its target by more than a threshold (default: 10%)
4. If imbalance detected, user is prompted to approve rebalancing

### Rebalance Execution

When user approves rebalancing:

1. **Planning Phase**: Calculates optimal transfers to achieve target distribution
   - Identifies which mints have excess tokens (sources)
   - Identifies which mints need tokens (targets)
   - Creates transfer plan to minimize number of transactions

2. **Quote Fetching Phase**: Pre-fetches all required quotes sequentially
   - Fetches mint quote for destination mint
   - Fetches melt quote for source mint
   - Validates fees against user-defined fee cap (default: 3%)
   - Skips transfers if fees exceed cap

3. **Execution Phase**: Executes transfers sequentially
   - Uses pre-fetched quotes to avoid duplicate requests
   - Executes melts directly via `wallet.melt()` with quote persistence
   - Continues with remaining transfers even if one fails
   - Provides real-time progress updates

4. **Completion**: Shows detailed results
   - Success notification if all transfers completed
   - Warning notification if some transfers skipped or failed
   - Includes counts and reasons for any issues

## User Interface

### Settings

- **Enable Auto-Rebalance**: Toggle to enable/disable the feature
- **Target Distribution**: Sliders for each mint to set desired percentage distribution
- **Fee Cap**: Maximum acceptable fee percentage for Lightning transfers (default: 3%)
- **Imbalance Threshold**: How far from target before rebalancing triggers (default: 10%)

### Rebalance Prompt Dialog

When imbalance detected, shows:
- Current vs target distribution for each mint
- List of proposed transfers with estimated fees
- "Balance Now" and "Skip" options
- During execution: progress indicator with transfer status

### Notifications

- Success: All transfers completed successfully
- Warning: Some transfers skipped (high fees) or failed
- Details include counts and specific reasons

## Technical Implementation

### Fee Protection

- Pre-fetches quotes before execution to validate fees
- Compares fee percentage against user-defined cap
- Skips individual transfers that exceed cap while continuing with others
- Logs skipped transfers with detailed fee information

### Error Handling

- Tracks skipped transfers separately from failed transfers
- Continues execution even if individual transfers fail
- Provides comprehensive error reporting via console and UI notifications
- Distinguishes between high-fee rejection and execution failure

### Crash Recovery

- All mint and melt quotes persisted to localStorage via existing `invoiceHistory` mechanism
- Rebalance transfers labeled for identification: `"Rebalance: mintA →"` and `"Rebalance: → mintB"`
- Bolt11 invoices properly tracked for melt operations
- Leverages existing wallet crash recovery infrastructure

### Timing

- Mint flow: Rebalance check runs after proofs added to store
- Receive flow: Rebalance check runs after token redemption completes
- Ensures balance calculations use current state, not stale data

### Internationalization

- All user-facing text internationalized via Vue I18n
- Translation keys under `rebalance` namespace
- Pluralization logic handled in JavaScript for flexibility
- Currently includes English translations, ready for additional languages

## Configuration

Default settings:
```typescript
autoRebalanceEnabled: false
autoRebalanceFeeCapPct: 3
autoRebalanceThresholdPct: 10
autoRebalanceTargets: {} // Per-mint percentages
```

All settings persisted to localStorage and survive app restarts.

title: Fix keyset rotation handling by merging instead of overwriting keysets
body:
Fixes #493

When a mint rotates its keyset ID (e.g., Minibits), the wallet was losing track of proofs with old keyset IDs. This happened because `fetchMintKeysets()` was overwriting the entire keysets array instead of merging new keysets with existing ones.

## Changes
- Modified `fetchMintKeysets()` in `src/stores/mints.ts` to merge keysets instead of overwriting them
- Old (inactive) keysets are now preserved when fetching new ones
- Existing keysets are updated with new information (e.g., active flag)
- New keysets are added to the collection
- Proofs with old keyset IDs remain valid and spendable

## Testing
The workaround mentioned in the issue (clicking on the mint to refresh keysets) should no longer be necessary. After this fix, proofs with old keyset IDs will automatically remain valid when a mint rotates its keysets.

title: Update keysets and mint info every hour before operations
body:
wallet did not fetch latest keysets as long as we don't "activate" the mint. we "activate" when we add it, or we switch from one mint to another. if a user has only one mint in their wallet, we activate that mint only once during setup and never again. if a mint rotates keysets in the mean time, the wallet doesn't know about this.

in this PR, we track the time when we updated the mint info and keyset and if `t > one_hour`, we fetch the mint info/keysets before we make operations with the mint.

title: fix: Update Docker build to use Node.js 22 and remove obsolete compose version
body:
The Docker build process was failing due to two issues:
1. **Node.js version incompatibility**: The Dockerfile used Node.js 20.10.0, but the `@cashu/cashu-ts@2.7.4` package requires Node.js >=22.4.0
2. **Obsolete Docker Compose syntax**: The `docker-compose.yaml` file contained an obsolete `version` field that triggered warnings

### Problem 1: Node.js Engine Mismatch

**Error Message:**
```
npm WARN EBADENGINE Unsupported engine {
npm WARN EBADENGINE   package: '@cashu/cashu-ts@2.7.4',
npm WARN EBADENGINE   required: { node: '>=22.4.0' },
npm WARN EBADENGINE   current: { node: 'v20.10.0', npm: '10.2.3' }
npm WARN EBADENGINE }
```

**Impact:**
- Build process failed during `npm install` step
- Network connection errors occurred as a side effect of the engine mismatch
- Docker container could not be built successfully

### Problem 2: Obsolete Docker Compose Version Field

**Warning Message:**
```
WARN[0000] /home/pookie/projects/cashu-projects/cashu.me/docker-compose.yaml: 
the attribute `version` is obsolete, it will be ignored, please remove it 
to avoid potential confusion
```

**Impact:**
- Warning message cluttered build output
- Using deprecated syntax that may be removed in future Docker Compose versions

### Problem 3: Docker Compose Command Syntax

**Error:**
```
bash: docker-compose: command not found
```

**Root Cause:**
- Docker Compose v2 uses `docker compose` (subcommand) instead of `docker-compose` (standalone command)
- The old `docker-compose` command is deprecated

## Solutions Applied

### Solution 1: Updated Node.js Version in Dockerfile

**File:** `cashu.me/Dockerfile`

**Change:**
```diff
- FROM node:20.10.0-bullseye AS builder
+ FROM node:22-bullseye AS builder
```

**Rationale:**
- Node.js 22.x is the current Active LTS version
- Meets the requirement for `@cashu/cashu-ts@2.7.4` (>=22.4.0)
- Using `node:22-bullseye` automatically uses the latest 22.x patch version
- Provides automatic security updates within the 22.x line

### Solution 2: Removed Obsolete Version Field

**File:** `cashu.me/docker-compose.yaml`

**Change:**
```diff
- version: "2"
  services:
```

**Rationale:**
- Docker Compose v2 no longer requires or uses the `version` field
- Removing it eliminates the warning and follows current best practices

### Solution 3: Updated Command Syntax

**Documentation:** `cashu.me/README.md`

The README already correctly uses `docker compose` (not `docker-compose`), which is the correct syntax for Docker Compose v2.

body: ### Summary Adds NIP-17 DM crash reporting system [Bugstr-TS](https://github.com/alltheseas/bugstr-ts) to cashu.me ### Screenshots via cashu.me local instance via coop NIP-17 DM receiving client ### Commits - chore: add Bugstr boot wiring (new boot file, env passthrough for BUGSTR_NPUB/BUGSTR_RELAYS) - feat: add Bugstr NIP-17 crash reporter (redaction + confirm hook, nostr-tools giftwrap send, Quasar toast) - chore: tidy deps for Bugstr POC (trimmed snstr-era extras) - chore: bump @typescript-eslint for TS 5.9 (eslint parser/plugin upgrade + lock update) ### Testing instructions: 1. Install deps: `npm install` 2. Run lint: `npm run lint` 3. Run tests: `npm test` 4. Manual Bugstr check: - Start dev with env: ```BUGSTR_NPUB=npub1... BUGSTR_RELAYS=wss://relay.damus.io,wss://nos.lol npm run dev``` (or pnpm quasar dev) - In browser console: ``` window.dispatchEvent(new ErrorEvent("error", { error: new Error("bugstr test crash") }));``` - Confirm prompt → OK; expect console logs “Bugstr: user confirmed send” and “Bugstr: send completed…”, toast “Bugstr crash report sent.” - Verify a NIP-17 DM arrived at the target npub via your [preferred NIP-17 app](https://github.com/nostrability/nostrability/issues/169). I utilize [coop](https://github.com/lumehq/coop) on desktop

title: [FEAT] Cairo Spending Conditions
body:
## Description
This PR implements Cairo spending conditions as specified in [NUTXX](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/288), enabling privacy-preserving arbitrary spending conditions through zero-knowledge proofs. Using the fork of [cashu-ts](https://github.com/cashubtc/cashu-ts/pull/364)

### Features:
  - Sending Cairo-locked tokens:
    - Cairo spending condition dialog UI (`CairoDialog.vue`)
    - Integration with existing token sending workflow
    - Cairo executable and expected output input handling
    - State management through dedicated Cairo store (cairo.ts)

  - Receiving Cairo-locked tokens:
    - Cairo receive dialog with proof generation (CairoReceiveDialog.vue)
    - Enhanced token receiving workflow with Cairo proof handling, analagous to the receiving workflow for `P2PK` locked tokens
